_meta.description: AdaptIQ knowledge base — DSA topic frames. Each topic is a frame with slots. The 'prerequisites' slot defines the prerequisite semantic net (a DAG). 'is_a' / 'part_of' / 'used_in' define the ontology relations. 'bkt_params' seed the Bayesian Knowledge Tracing engine.

bkt_params_legend.p_learn: P(transition to mastered) per practice opportunity

common_misconceptions.text: Believing insertion/deletion in the middle of an array is O(1); it is O(n) because elements must shift.
Confusing O(1) access by index with searching for a value, which is O(n) in an unsorted array.

topics.name: Linked Lists
concepts: O(1) insertion/deletion at a known node

common_misconceptions.text: Assuming linked lists support O(1) indexed access like arrays; reaching the k-th node is O(k).
Thinking insertion is always O(1); it is O(1) only once you already hold the node/position, otherwise you pay O(n) to find it.

topics.name: Recursion
concepts: the call stack and stack frames

common_misconceptions.text: Forgetting or mis-stating the base case, leading to infinite recursion / stack overflow.
Assuming recursion has no space cost; each pending call consumes a stack frame, so depth d uses O(d) space.

topics.name: Stacks & Queues
concepts: the call stack as a stack

common_misconceptions.text: Mixing up LIFO and FIFO — expecting a stack to return the oldest element or a queue to return the newest.
Trying to access the middle element directly; stacks and queues only expose their ends in O(1).

topics.name: Sorting Algorithms
concepts: time complexity: O(n^2) vs O(n log n)

common_misconceptions.text: Believing quick sort is always O(n log n); its worst case is O(n^2) with poor pivot choices.
Assuming all sorts are stable; quick sort and heap sort are not stable by default.
Thinking merge sort is in-place; standard merge sort needs O(n) auxiliary space.

topics.name: Hashing & Hash Tables
concepts: average O(1) vs worst-case O(n) operations

common_misconceptions.text: Believing hash table lookups are always O(1); worst case degrades to O(n) under heavy collisions.
Expecting hash tables to preserve insertion or sorted order; they do not, by design.

topics.name: Trees & Binary Trees
concepts: root, parent, child, leaf, height, depth
complete vs full vs balanced trees

common_misconceptions.text: Confusing height (longest path to a leaf) with depth (distance from the root).
Assuming every binary tree is a binary search tree; BST requires the ordering property.

topics.name: Binary Search Trees
concepts: balanced vs skewed trees and why balance matters
self-balancing variants (AVL, red-black) at a high level

common_misconceptions.text: Believing BST operations are always O(log n); a skewed BST degrades to O(n).
Not realizing that an inorder traversal of a BST produces elements in sorted order.

topics.name: Heaps & Priority Queues
concepts: insert and extract-min/max in O(log n)

common_misconceptions.text: Assuming a heap is fully sorted; it only guarantees the heap property between parent and children, not a total order.
Thinking extract-min is O(1); only peek is O(1), extraction is O(log n) due to re-heapify.

topics.name: Graphs
concepts: vertices, edges, directed vs undirected, weighted
adjacency list vs adjacency matrix trade-offs
shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford) at a high level

common_misconceptions.text: Swapping BFS and DFS — BFS uses a queue and explores level by level; DFS uses a stack/recursion and goes deep first.
Using an adjacency matrix for sparse graphs, wasting O(V^2) space where an adjacency list uses O(V+E).

topics.name: Dynamic Programming
concepts: classic problems: knapsack, LCS, coin change

common_misconceptions.text: Applying a greedy choice where DP is required — greedy fails when local optima do not compose into a global optimum.
Believing DP is just recursion with a cache; the essential ingredients are optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems.
Failing to identify a correct state definition, leading to a recurrence that is wrong or exponential.
